headline: Nothing survived. The best of 4 tested combinations was VWAP on AAPL at 3.9 out of 10.
summary: 4 indicator-and-stock combinations were tested this week. Each was scored from 1 to 10 on whether it still made money on data it had never seen, after paying realistic trading costs. None scored 8 or above, so none survived convincingly. 4 of 4 finished with a positive Sharpe ratio after costs — but a positive Sharpe is a low bar, and none of them beat simply buying and holding the same stock. The median score was 3.7. A low median is the expected result rather than a broken test: most published indicator backtests do not subtract trading costs or check performance on unseen data, and doing both is what removes the apparent edge.
